candidates.review_note: A legal word over buttons <=j contains j at most once, hence is either a smaller word or L j R. Let G_j=sum A^length for all such words including empty: G_j=G_(j-1)*(I+A*G_(j-1)). Maintain B=A*G, starting B=A, with B_next=B+B^2. For each query maintain the start-row and end-column of words starting/ending at the specified button, measured with length-1 transitions once that button exists. Each is multiplied by F_j=I+B except at its own button level; earlier levels accumulate the smaller-word G factor. New words whose maximum is j contribute identity for a=b=j, one A for exactly one endpoint j, or two A factors connecting nonempty left/right words for j>max(a,b). This counts every legal word once without requiring matrix inverses. Packed 72-bit integer convolution extracts exact modular matrix/vector dot products: at most 60 products of residues below 1e9+7 cannot carry between lanes. No floating arithmetic or probabilistic identity assumption. Endpoint-equal maximum contributions use the original room unit vector because that side is empty, as verified by the published sample regression. For distinct endpoint buttons, the sum telescopes via G_j-G_(j-1)=A*G_(j-1)^2 to A times the product of all F_j except the two endpoint levels; compute it directly without inverses. Equal endpoints retain the disjoint maximum-button sum, carrying A in the row and column to avoid repeated A multiplications.
